enquiry: Our juice bottling line sometimes fills batches that customers describe as tasting off. We were told UV/Vis spectroscopy is extremely sensitive, so we want to put it on the filler and let it reject bad batches automatically. We do not know what causes the off taste.

clarification_questions.question: What goes wrong today when batches are found to taste off: at what point is it detected, what does it cost, and what decision should real-time data drive?
clarification_questions.why: Clarifies the stakeholder pain and whether an automatic reject is the right decision to support.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Off-taste is detected late by customers or sensory checks; the decision is to be defined after lab screening.

clarification_questions.question: Do you know which compound or property causes the off taste (e.g. a specific degradation product, contaminant, or oxidation marker), and roughly at what concentration it becomes noticeable?
clarification_questions.why: UV/Vis needs a defined absorbing species; sensitivity alone does not show selectivity for the taste cause.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Cause unknown; lab screening establishes whether a UV/Vis-absorbing target exists and whether it is at ppm or % level.

clarification_questions.question: Is the juice clear, turbid (e.g. with pulp) or opaque, and does its optical appearance vary between batches or products?
clarification_questions.why: Optical properties decide the probe geometry (transmission, transflection or ATR) and the signal quality.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Treated as clear liquid for planning; lab screening confirms optical behaviour.

clarification_questions.question: How does the juice vary between batches (formulation, pulp content, temperature, cleaning or sterilisation steps) and where on the filler would a sensor sit?
clarification_questions.why: Batch-to-batch variation can change the spectrum and invalidate a calibration; the sensor position sets the usable measurement.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Variation unknown; lab screening on representative batches is required before any in-line trial.

clarification_questions.question: Where exactly would the sensor be installed, how far is the analyzer from that point, and do you have existing optical fibers?
clarification_questions.why: Distance and fiber type determine the feasible wavelength range and whether remote measurement is possible.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Installation point and distance unknown; no fiber assumed.

clarification_questions.question: How is off taste verified today (sensory panel, lab analysis such as GC or HPLC), and how accurate and frequent is that reference?
clarification_questions.why: A reference method is needed to test whether any spectral signal correlates with off taste.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Reference method unknown; sensory or lab reference must be established before modelling.

clarification_questions.question: What accuracy, response time and budget do you need for an automatic reject decision, and is a reject decision required in real time per bottle or per batch?
clarification_questions.why: Sets whether an in-line analyzer, a sampling approach or an offline test fits the need.
clarification_questions.assumption_if_unanswered: Requirements unknown; lab screening comes first before choosing an in-line configuration.

Compare prediction error, bias and ability to follow changes against client-agreed requirements.

flags_before_revision.detail: overstated: The claim says a recipe or matrix change "can invalidate any calibration". DOCX §5 only says NIR and Raman calibrations are specific to the matrix. The word "any" generalises beyond what the page states. Fix: State that a change in juice recipe or matrix can invalidate calibrations that were built for the original matrix, and that the calibration must be checked against the new matrix.

not_supported: S01 p.7 mentions process turbulence, sample inhomogeneity and morphological factors. It does not mention pulp, clarity or temperature, and it does not say these can mimic composition changes. Fix: Limit the risk to what the page supports, for example: process turbulence and sample inhomogeneity must be considered when selecting a measurement technique, and may affect the measurement.

rule_hints: nominal_range_not_instrument_range: A nominal method range is not the usable range of a specific instrument, fiber or probe. [DOCX §3; DOCX §5]

geometry_follows_optics: Clear liquids suit transmission or transflection; opaque, concentrated or powder samples suit diffuse reflection; highly absorbing or 'black' liquids suit ATR. [S01 Table 1 (p.6); S01 p.16; S01 p.17-18]
do_not_invent: Do not invent measured results, accuracy, detection limits, response times, fiber lengths, product codes or prices, client facts, or guarantees. [DOCX §3]
insufficient_information_is_valid: If the known facts cannot justify a method choice, say so, ask the deciding questions and propose the next step. [DOCX §3]
